title: The Spotlight Effect

scenes.vo: That embarrassing thing you did? Almost nobody noticed. Science says so.

scenes.text: Students wore a super *cringey* T-shirt into class
scenes.vo: Scientists asked students to walk into a room wearing a really cringey T-shirt.

scenes.text: They guessed: *half* the room would notice
scenes.vo: The students guessed that about half the room would notice the shirt.
The real answer? Only about one in four people did.
This is called the spotlight effect. You feel like there's a spotlight on you all the time. But there isn't.
Everyone else is too busy worrying about their own hair, their own outfit and their own mistakes.

scenes.text: Next time you cringe, cut it in *half*. That's closer to the truth.
scenes.vo: So next time you feel embarrassed, cut it in half. That's much closer to the truth.

caption:
You're not being watched nearly as much as you think. 🔦 It's called the spotlight effect.

Send this to the friend who still overthinks something from last year 😅
source: Gilovich, T., Medvec, V. H. & Savitsky, K. (2000). The spotlight effect in social judgment. Journal of Personality and Social Psychology, 78(2).
